outcomes.text: Understand museums as places that preserve, exhibit and interpret historically, culturally, artistically or scientifically significant objects.
Explore museum artefacts and what they reveal about history and culture.
Investigate how curation and contextual information influence the interpretation of displayed objects.
Examine museum narratives and archives, including which perspectives or objects are included or omitted.
Consider ways museums inform and engage their audiences.
Explore the personal or cultural significance of an object from a collection.
Explore water creatively as a subject shaped by changing physical qualities and symbolic meanings.
Investigate bodies of water, including rivers, seas, streams, lakes, estuaries, reservoirs, canals, ponds, pools and puddles.
Explore water’s changing states and its relationship with weather.
Investigate the absence of water, including drought and dryness.
Explore forms of rainfall and moving water, including hail, waterfalls, waves, tides and dripping taps.
Investigate underwater environments, aquatic life, plants, fish and marine ecosystems.
Communicate ideas through the use of line.
Communicate ideas through the use of tone.
Communicate ideas through the use of form.
Communicate ideas through the use of shape.
Communicate ideas through the use of pictorial space.
Communicate ideas through the use of composition.
Communicate ideas through colour theory.
Communicate ideas through semantics and semiotics.
Communicate ideas through harmony and balance.
Continually evaluate and test work to check that it meets the brief.
Use feedback and evaluation to develop and improve designs.
Evaluate how successfully the design meets the brief.
Evaluate how successfully visual language is used.
Evaluate the interpretation and realisation of ideas.
Recognise and incorporate contextual and sociological influences.
Recognise and incorporate relevant ethical considerations.
Test responsive designs across different devices and changing online conditions.
Test user experience by assessing ease of use and satisfaction of user needs.
Test user interface interactions and the effectiveness of visual layout.
Test whether the most appropriate technology is used and technological advances are explored.
Test accessibility by making designs inclusive for diverse users, including disabled users and varied cultures.
Test environmental impact by avoiding harmful materials and using efficient, sustainable processes.
Test and consider the data trail users create online.
Test online ethics, data protection and safeguarding to protect users from sensitive, harmful or offensive content.
Create storyboards and images using photography, modelling, drawing and/or illustration.
Plan and prepare the equipment and resources needed for moving-image work.
Construct images using scale, composition and formal visual elements.
Research filming locations or site-specific settings when appropriate.
Brief participants or actors and undertake casting.
Produce scripts and shot lists.
Develop characters or models for animation.
Use suitable software for moving-image production.
Select, edit and manipulate video sequences.
Maintain production records using appropriate specialist terminology.
Use suitable equipment, such as cameras, lenses, filters, projectors, lighting and props.
Communicate ideas and meaning visually.
Use feedback to evaluate progress and communicate meaning through images.
Choose an appropriate moving-image style or genre for a theme or brief.
Understand the intended audience and how the completed moving-image work will be viewed.

topics.title: Games design and mobile and multimedia applications

outcomes.text: Generate ideas through drawing, concept art and/or narrative image-making.
Storyboard and pitch ideas and concepts.
Understand and apply a suitable workflow strategy.
Plan and prepare the equipment and resources required.
Construct images using scale, composition and formal visual elements.
Explore role-play, online or mobile games as games-design forms.
Design applications using user journeys and page layouts.
Develop characters and write scripts.
Use viewpoints, timing and pace effectively.
Direct, produce, edit and complete post-production processes.
Keep records using relevant specialist technical terminology.
Choose formats and resolutions appropriate to how the outcome will be viewed.
Use web-based hosting or storage services for online media.
Communicate ideas and meaning visually.
Use appropriate available software; coding is needed only when integral to the outcome.
Ensure prototype platform, MMO and RPG concepts use age-appropriate content and themes.
Use feedback to evaluate progress and communicate meaning through the work.
Select suitable styles, genres and platforms for the brief and intended outcome.
Make audience-focused choices considering bandwidth, responsiveness, processing power and screen size to improve accessibility and usability.
Understand how reused digital content must suit the ways different platforms are accessed.
Understand how the final product will be presented and how users will interact with it.
